title: Ancient Egyptian Slavery
locator: pp.41-66; esp. terminology caveats, Third Intermediate Period sparse documentation, entry/sale overview
claim_fitness: Strong for Egyptian slavery/coerced-labour distinctions and sparse Third Intermediate documentation; broad Egypt-level evidence, not Karnak-specific
access_limitation: Open-access chapter read in HTML; not a target-specific Karnak study
dependency_note: Independent modern synthesis; do not convert broad Third Intermediate attestations into Karnak practice.

title: Slavery and Servitude
locator: Abstract/full UEE article; first-millennium change and semantic range of ḥm / bꜣk
claim_fitness: Strong for warning that servant/slave terminology is unstable and first-millennium servitude differs from New Kingdom slavery; not target-specific
access_limitation: UEE article accessible; source is broad historical synthesis
dependency_note: Overlaps conceptually with Karev but is a distinct specialist synthesis.

title: The Ancient Egyptian Economy, chapter 5: The Third Intermediate Period
locator: pp.142-172; Menkheperre/Henuttawy Amun-oracular property settlements; perpetual service/property discussion
claim_fitness: Strong for Amun-priestly near-anchor property/service relations; insufficient for Temple-of-Amun internal slave labour because institutional owner/locus differ
access_limitation: Cambridge bibliographic metadata plus accessible text mirror used for detailed passage; clearest perpetual-service personnel derive from an Abydos-linked transaction
dependency_note: Critical locus control: Amun-priestly family/legal environment is not identical to Temple-of-Amun workforce.

title: Settlement Development and Built Remains of the Third Intermediate Period
locator: pp.86-154; Thebes section, Twenty-first-Dynasty Menkheperre stela and Asiatic domestic population inside Great Amun temple walls
claim_fitness: Strong for near-anchor population inside/around Great Amun enclosure; status is unspecified and unfit for slave/unfree classification
access_limitation: Cambridge chapter text accessible; no slave-status classification supplied for the population
dependency_note: Foreign/Asiatic identity must not be treated as status evidence.

title: Stele der Verbannten / Banishment Stela
locator: Twenty-first Dynasty; Menkheperre; bꜣk.w group banished to oasis and recalled; bibliography includes Jansen-Winkeln 2007 and von Beckerath 1968
claim_fitness: Strong for bꜣk.w terminology and coercive banishment/amnesty in Amun/Karnak political context; insufficient for slave property or productive labour status
access_limitation: Primary Egyptian not independently translated; relied on TLA metadata and specialist translation/discussion
dependency_note: All editions/translations of this stela are one textual evidence family.

title: Marginalized Textile Producers in New Kingdom Egypt
locator: New Kingdom textile labour; captives/enslaved workers; mrt and Amun-temple workshop context
claim_fitness: Strong for New Kingdom captive/enslaved temple production and status complexity; temporally earlier than 1000 BCE
access_limitation: Full HTML article accessible; evidence belongs to New Kingdom context
dependency_note: Overlaps primary/source traditions with Valerio and other New Kingdom captive studies; not independent near-anchor evidence.

title: Prisioneros de guerra (Reino Nuevo, Egipto)
locator: §3.2 and §4.4; New Kingdom prisoner allocation, Temple of Amun-Ra at Karnak as major beneficiary
claim_fitness: Strong for New Kingdom allocation of prisoners to Amun-Ra temple labour; not evidence of continuity to 1000 BCE
access_limitation: Spanish translation of specialist-authored French contribution; New Kingdom only
dependency_note: Materially overlaps New Kingdom royal/temple prisoner evidence with Galczynski; count as one broad evidence family for continuity purposes.
